verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents Airbyte Core as its open-source product. It can be self-hosted locally with abctl on any Docker host, or deployed into any Kubernetes cluster, and a community user confirms their company self-hosts it. An older install failure report (docker-compose era) and a freemium-licensing remark do not concretely contradict the currently documented self-hosting paths. Missing for 10: clear evidence of which paid features (e.g., SSO/RBAC) are available in self-hosted Core, and recent hands-on corroboration of the current abctl/Kubernetes install.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: This quickstart guides you through deploying a local instance of Airbyte Core, Airbyte's open source product.
abctl makes it easy to run Airbyte anywhere Docker is running.
This installation guide walks through how to deploy Airbyte into any kubernetes cluster.
We use airbyte at my company, although we self-host it.
